articles.summary: Gold and silver mining equities have outperformed the underlying metals year-to-date, supported by improving margins, stronger free cash flow potential and renewed investor interest in the operational leverage miners can offer. Watch the webcast replay to learn why Sprott Portfolio Managers Maria Smirnova and Justin Tolman believe mining equities may have entered a new phase of leadership, and what that could mean for precious metals allocations.
articles.title: The Miners Take the Lead: What's Driving Gold & Silver Equities

articles.summary: Kenny Zhu joins Proactive to discuss the forces shaping silver’s outlook, from monetary conditions and industrial demand to persistent annual supply deficits. Zhu explains why demand from electronics, AI infrastructure and China’s manufacturing sector may support the silver market, and why Sprott likes silver miners for their leverage, margin potential and attractive valuations.
articles.title: Silver’s Next Rally and Why Miners Could Outperform

articles.summary: Robotics is expanding across manufacturing, logistics, healthcare and defense, relying on rare earths in its magnets, sensors and electronics. As robots become more advanced and widely adopted, their increasing use of rare earth-intensive components is set to drive long-term demand for these materials. We examine why resilient, ex-China mine-to-magnet supply chains are increasingly strategic.
articles.title: The Rare Earths Powering the Next Wave of Robotics

articles.summary: Uranium miners have sold off sharply even as spot uranium prices remain firm and long-term contract prices reach record levels. We examine why liquidity pressures—not weakening uranium fundamentals—appear to be driving the disconnect, while nuclear expansion, tightening inventories and slow mine supply continue to support the long-term positive outlook.
articles.title: Uranium Miners: A Liquidity Shock, Not a Broken Thesis

articles.summary: Gold miners have entered a new era—one defined by stronger balance sheets, greater capital discipline and record earnings, yet valuations still reflect the industry’s past. At the same time, a growing scarcity of high-quality gold reserves could increase the strategic value of gold miners capable of replacing and developing economic ounces.
articles.title: Gold Mining 2.0: Are Investors Looking Through an Outdated Lens?

articles.summary: Gold held firm in September as real yields surged, suggesting investors are increasingly focused on fiscal strain and reserve diversification. We examine why rising Treasury yields can deepen the fiscal challenge and why gold’s role outside the sovereign liability structure matters. We also assess silver’s rate headwinds, resilient Chinese demand and industrial support.
articles.title: Gold Holds Its Ground as Real Yields Surge
